canonicalExplanation.summary: **Custom properties** (`--color-text: #1f2937;`) are variables that live **in the cascade**: they're set on elements, inherited by descendants, and read with `var(--color-text)` at the moment each element's styles are computed. Change the value on a parent — like `.theme-dark` — and every component inside picks up the new value. A small set of them for colours, spacing and type is a **design-token layer**.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
You need a dark theme. Hunting through 40 components for every `#1f2937` would take a day and miss some. With tokens, you change a handful of values in one scope and the whole interface follows. A --color-text token changes inside a dark theme scope, and every consuming component receives the scoped value. In this lesson you'll create a small color, spacing and typography token layer and trace an override.

```predict
{"question": "`:root { --gap: 8px }` and `.roomy { --gap: 24px }`. A card inside `.roomy` uses `padding: var(--gap)`. What padding?", "options": ["8px — custom properties are global constants", "24px — it inherits the nearest value in its ancestry"], "answer": 1, "why": "Custom properties cascade and inherit like other properties. The nearest ancestor that sets --gap wins."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Specificity and source order**, **Text and page semantics**, and **Inheritance, initial and computed values** — custom properties inherit.

examples.title: A dark theme through one token
examples.situation: A --color-text token changes inside a dark theme scope and every consuming component receives the scoped value.
walkthrough: **Dark theme scope:** `.theme-dark { --color-text: #f3f4f6 }` on a section's wrapper.
**Trace:** inspect a card inside it; DevTools will show --color-text inherited from .theme-dark, so it renders light text.
examples.result: Every component inside the dark scope gets light text without editing any component rule.

examples.title: The hard-coded straggler
examples.situation: After switching to tokens, one button stays dark-on-dark in the dark theme.
walkthrough: Its rule still says `color: #1f2937` instead of `var(--color-text)`.
Hard-coded values ignore the scoped tokens.
Fix: replace it with the token; search the stylesheet for raw hex values to catch others.
examples.result: The button follows the theme like every other component.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Custom properties are globally fixed constants evaluated before the cascade.
misconceptions.correction: Custom properties participate in the cascade and inherit: each element uses the value from its nearest ancestor (or itself), resolved when its styles are computed. That's what lets a scope like .theme-dark override them.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, why did the card get 24px?

analogy.example: Tokens are like **dimmer switches wired to a room**: every lamp in the room (component) reads the room's switch (nearest ancestor). Change the switch in one room, and only that room's lamps change.
limitations: Real wiring is fixed; CSS scopes can be added anywhere.
A lamp with its own hard-wired bulb (hard-coded value) ignores the switch.

steps.explanation: The root defines the default text token.
The --color-text token changes inside a dark theme scope.
Every consuming component receives the scoped value.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing a token override. Step 1, Default token: --color-text is #1f2937. The root defines the default text token. Step 2, Scoped override: .theme-dark --color-text is #f3f4f6. The --color-text token changes inside a dark theme scope. Step 3, Consumer: card color is #f3f4f6. Every consuming component receives the scoped value.

faded.prompt: For "A dark theme through one token", explain how the --color-text token changes inside a dark theme scope and how every consuming component receives the scoped value.
expectedEvidence: Names the example "A dark theme through one token": a --color-text token.
It changes inside a dark theme scope, .theme-dark.
Every consuming component receives the scoped value via var().

nearTransfer.prompt: Create tokens --space-1 to --space-4 and --radius, then use them in a button. Make a `.compact` scope that shrinks the spacing.
expectedEvidence: Tokens defined and consumed with var().

farTransfer.prompt: Convert a small stylesheet's colours and spacings to tokens, add a dark theme scope, and verify in DevTools that every component follows it. List any hard-coded stragglers you fixed.
expectedEvidence: All colours and spacings use tokens.
Dark theme works everywhere; stragglers listed and fixed.

remediation.explanation: When a token looks wrong, inspect the element and find **which ancestor set it** in the Styles pane. Then check the rule uses var() and not a hard-coded value.

recap.summary: To create a small color, spacing and typography token layer, define custom properties on :root, consume them with var() (with fallbacks where useful), and override them in scopes like .theme-dark. Trace an override in DevTools — tokens cascade and inherit, they aren't fixed constants.
